nodes.title: What can and cannot be globalized
nodes.statement: The ε-invariant cannot be globalized by an adelic divisor on S/ℤ in the manner of Φ_S: its non-archimedean component is nontrivial while its archimedean component is identically zero, which is incompatible with the continuity of total Green functions on the hybrid space S^an over M(ℤ); hence neither can δ (since Ξ_S globalizes δ + ε). Yuan asserts, without proof, that a finer analysis of Theorem 3.10 describes the boundary growth of φ (and, with Ξ in place of Φ, of the archimedean δ) on complex moduli in terms of the graph data of Φ̃ (resp. δ + ε).
hypotheses: Arithmetic base k = ℤ.
proofSteps: A total Green function is continuous on S^an, whose archimedean and non-archimedean parts meet along the trivial-norm locus; a function vanishing on the archimedean part but equal to ε(Γ_v)log e_v on divisorial non-archimedean points cannot be continuous at the trivial norm in general (Yuan Remark 4.13(1)).
The growth statements (Remarks 3.11 and 4.13(2)) are recorded as asserted consequences, not targets proved here (gap).
acceptance: Φ_S and Ξ_S exist over ℤ; E_S exists only over a field.

sources.match: Records that ε and δ cannot be globalized and that the method describes the boundary growth of φ and δ; items PAPER-YUAN-26/278–280.

nodes.title: Uniform positivity of φ on compact Riemann surfaces
nodes.statement: For each g > 1 there is c₀(g) > 0 with φ(C) ≥ c₀(g) for every compact Riemann surface C of genus g. On the complex points of a fine full-level moduli space M_{g,N} (N ≥ 3), φ is continuous, positive and tends to +∞ at the boundary of the stable compactification.
proofSteps: Positivity at each point: AH.10/local-phi-invariant(2).
Continuity on M_{g,N}(ℂ): φ is the Green function of Φ̃ over (ℂ, |·|) (AH.1/complex-base), continuous on M^an.

Boundary growth: the geometric bound Φ − Δ/39 ≥ 0 over ℂ (AH.10/phi-bound applied to the universal family over M_{g,N,ℂ} with its van Geemen–Oort stable compactification) means the Green function of Φ̃ dominates (1/39)·(the Green function of Δ), which tends to +∞ at the boundary.
Compactness of the stable compactification then gives a positive minimum (Yuan Theorem 3.10 proof, pp. 57–58, with the corrections of source issue E5).
acceptance: For g = 2 the bound agrees in shape with de Jong's asymptotics (Yuan p. 56).

sources.match: Proves a uniform positive lower bound for φ on compact Riemann surfaces of genus g by showing φ → ∞ at the boundary of moduli through the adelic divisor Φ̃; items PAPER-YUAN-26/109–111.

nodes.title: Bigness of ⟨ω_a, ω_a⟩ in the geometric case
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, S quasi-projective normal integral over k and π : X → S smooth of genus g > 1 with maximal variation (StableReductionPartII MC.6/maximal-variation). Then P = π_*⟨w, w⟩ is nef and big on S/k. When dim S = 0 every adelic line bundle on S/k is declared nef and big.
hypotheses: k a field; maximal variation.
proofSteps: Nefness: AH.9/nefness-omega-a.

Pass to a finite cover with a stable compactification (StableReductionPartII MC.6/stable-compactification-exists) and normalize; bigness of nef bundles is invariant under finite covers (AH.4/finite-cover-bigness).

By AH.10/hodge-lower-decomposition, P = cλ_S̄ + A + O(B) with c > 0; λ_S̄ is nef and big under maximal variation (StableReductionPartII MC.6/maximal-variation-hodge, via the Torelli map to the minimal compactification), so cλ_S̄ + A is nef and big, and adding O(B) effective keeps bigness.
acceptance: For S a curve with a non-isotrivial family, P has positive degree.

sources.locator: Theorem 3.2, p. 40; proof after Remark 3.9, pp. 55–56
sources.match: Proves bigness of π_*⟨ω_a, ω_a⟩ over a field from Theorem 3.8 and the bigness of the Hodge bundle under maximal variation; items PAPER-YUAN-26/68, 106, 107.

nodes.title: Bigness of ⟨ω_a, ω_a⟩ in the arithmetic case
nodes.statement: Let S be flat quasi-projective normal integral over ℤ, π : X → S smooth of genus g > 1 with maximal variation, d = dim S and P = π_*⟨w, w⟩. Then P = (2/(3g − 1))O(c₀) + nef + effective with c₀ = c₀(g) of AH.11/uniform-phi-bound, where O(c₀) is the trivial bundle on Spec ℤ with ‖1‖ = e^{−c₀}; hence P^d ≥ (2c₀/(3g − 1))·(P|_{S_ℚ/ℚ})^{d−1} > 0, and P is nef and big on S/ℤ.
hypotheses: k = ℤ; maximal variation.
proofSteps: By AH.10/triple-pairing, P = (2/(3g − 1))O(Φ_S) + nef.

Φ_S − c₀ is effective: its Green function is φ at archimedean points (≥ c₀ by AH.11/uniform-phi-bound) and φ ≥ 0 at non-archimedean points (AH.10/local-phi-invariant(3)) — the latter is the step source issue PAPER-YUAN-26/E6 says the paper uses without citing.
Expand P^d = P^{d−1}·((2/(3g−1))O(c₀) + nef + eff) ≥ (2c₀/(3g − 1))(P|_{S_ℚ})^{d−1}, and (P|_{S_ℚ})^{d−1} > 0 by AH.11/geometric-bigness over ℚ; conclude by AH.4/hilbert-samuel-siu.
acceptance: For d = 1 (S = open in Spec O_K) the statement is P ≥ (2/(3g − 1))c₀ > 0 in degree.

sources.locator: Proof of the arithmetic case of Theorem 3.2, p. 57; §1.4, p. 14

nodes.title: Bigness of the admissible canonical bundle
nodes.statement: Let k be ℤ or a field, S flat quasi-projective normal integral over k and π : X → S smooth of genus g > 1 with maximal variation. Then ω_{X/S,a} is nef and big on X/k, and π_*⟨ω_a, ω_a⟩ is nef and big on S/k.

proofSteps: Nefness: AH.9/nefness-omega-a.
Bigness of P = π_*⟨w, w⟩: AH.11/geometric-bigness or AH.11/arithmetic-bigness.

Bigness of w: 4g(g − 1)w = i_ω^*Θ̄ + π^*P (AH.9/canonical-theta-identities(1)). With d = dim S, expand (i_ω^*Θ̄ + π^*P)^{d+1}: all terms are ≥ 0 by nefness, and the term (d + 1)·i_ω^*Θ̄·(π^*P)^d equals (d + 1)·a·P^d > 0, where a = 4g(g − 1)(2g − 2) is the generic fibre degree of i_ω^*Θ̄ (AH.3/projection-formulas); conclude by AH.4/hilbert-samuel-siu (Yuan p. 40).
acceptance: For S = Spec K a global field this is Zhang's ω_a² > 0 for non-isotrivial curves (the function-field case needs non-isotriviality, which is maximal variation over the constant field).

nodes.title: Potential bigness and relative powers
nodes.statement: Let k be ℤ or a field, S flat quasi-projective normal integral over k, Y integral and π : Y → S projective flat with geometrically integral generic fibre of relative dimension e. For m ≥ 1 let Y^m_{/S} = Y ×_S ··· ×_S Y (Y⁰ = S); it is integral. For L̄ ∈ P̂ic(Y/k) put m⊠L̄ = Σᵢ pᵢ^*L̄ on Y^m_{/S}. L̄ is potentially big over S if m⊠L̄ is big on Y^m_{/S} for some m ≥ 1.

nodes.title: Intersections and Deligne pairings on relative powers
nodes.statement: In the setting of AH.12/potential-bigness, let L̄ be nef integrable with a = deg(L_η^e) > 0 and d = dim S. (1) For nonnegative r₁, …, r_m with Σrᵢ = em + 1, (π_m)_*⟨(p₁^*L̄)^{r₁}, …, (p_m^*L̄)^{r_m}⟩ vanishes unless (r₁, …, r_m) is a permutation of (e + 1, e, …, e), in which case it is a^{m−1}π_*⟨L̄^{e+1}⟩; hence (π_m)_*⟨(m⊠L̄)^{em+1}⟩ is a positive multiple of π_*⟨L̄^{e+1}⟩. (2) For m ≥ d, the top intersection (p₁^*L̄)^{e+1}···(p_d^*L̄)^{e+1}(p_{d+1}^*L̄)^e···(p_m^*L̄)^e on Y^m_{/S} equals a^{m−d}(π_*⟨L̄^{e+1}⟩)^d (with the dimension-zero convention).
hypotheses: L̄ nef integrable; a > 0.
proofSteps: Factor π_m through the projections and apply AH.3/projection-formulas: a factor with rᵢ ≤ e − 1 kills the pairing (fibre degree zero), a factor with rᵢ = e contributes a, a factor with rᵢ = e + 1 contributes π_*⟨L̄^{e+1}⟩, and at most one rᵢ can exceed e (Yuan pp. 62–63).
(2) by induction on d using (1) and the composition formula.
acceptance: m = 1: (1) is tautological; e = 0 gives the multinomial expansion of (Σ pᵢ^*L̄)^{m+…}.

nodes.title: The criterion for potential bigness
nodes.statement: In the setting of AH.12/potential-bigness, let L̄ be nef with positive fibre degree a = deg(L_η^e) > 0 and M̄ = π_*⟨L̄^{e+1}⟩. The following are equivalent: (1) M̄ is big on S; (2) m⊠L̄ is big on Y^m_{/S} for every m ≥ dim S; (3) L̄ is potentially big over S.
hypotheses: L̄ nef; a > 0.
proofSteps: (1) ⇒ (2): m⊠L̄ is nef, so bigness is positivity of (m⊠L̄)^{d+em}; expand and keep the term b_m of AH.12/relative-power-intersections(2), which is a^{m−d}M̄^d > 0 by Hilbert–Samuel, all other terms being ≥ 0 by nefness.
(2) ⇒ (3) is trivial.

(3) ⇒ (1): (π_m)_*⟨(m⊠L̄)^{em+1}⟩ is a positive multiple of M̄ (AH.12/relative-power-intersections(1)); Deligne pairings of nef big bundles are nef big (AH.4/deligne-positivity(1)) after adding a small relatively ample perturbation, and finite covers preserve bigness.
acceptance: For dim S = 0 (the paper convention) every L̄ with a > 0 is potentially big.

sources.match: Proves the equivalence of bigness of the Deligne pairing, bigness of all box powers m ≥ dim S, and potential bigness; item PAPER-YUAN-26/115.

nodes.title: The product-grid degree bound
nodes.statement: Let C be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over an algebraically closed field F, Z ⊊ C^m closed of codimension d > 0, N a degree-one line bundle and Σ ⊂ C(F) with Σ^m ⊂ Z(F). Then Σ is finite and |Σ| ≤ (deg_{m⊠N} Z)^{1/d}, the degree summing over all irreducible components (of possibly different dimensions).
hypotheses: C smooth projective connected over F = F̄; Z proper closed of codimension d.
proofSteps: Induction on m by intersecting with fibres of the projections; Bézout-type bound for products of points (Yuan Lemma 4.3).
Apply first to finite subsets of Σ, then conclude finiteness of Σ from the uniform bound (the correction of source issue PAPER-YUAN-26/E22).
acceptance: m = 1, Z a finite set of n points: |Σ| ≤ n.

sources.match: Proves |Σ| ≤ (deg Z)^{1/d} for Σ^m ⊂ Z; item PAPER-YUAN-26/122.

nodes.title: Potential bigness of theta pullbacks
nodes.statement: Let k be ℤ or a field, S flat quasi-projective normal integral over k, π : X → S smooth of genus g > 1 with maximal variation, J, Θ̄, X_J = J ×_S X, J_J = J ×_S J, q₁ : X_J → J and τ(y, x) = (y, y + (2g − 2)x − ω) as in AH.9. (1) For α of positive relative degree, π_*⟨i_α^*Θ̄, i_α^*Θ̄⟩ is nef and big on S, so i_α^*Θ̄ is potentially big on X/S. (2) With X_X = X ×_S X, J_X = X ×_S J, i_Δ(x, y) = (x, y − x) and Θ̄_X = p₂^*Θ̄, p₁_*⟨i_Δ^*Θ̄_X, i_Δ^*Θ̄_X⟩ is nef and big on X, so i_Δ^*Θ̄_X is potentially big on X_X/X. (3) q₁_*⟨τ^*Θ̄_J, τ^*Θ̄_J⟩ is nef and big on J, so τ^*Θ̄_J is potentially big on X_J/J. (4) If Y is a quasi-projective k-variety with a generically finite Y → J whose image T in S has T → M_{g,k} generically finite, then q₁_*⟨τ^*Θ̄_J, τ^*Θ̄_J⟩|_Y is nef and big on Y and τ^*Θ̄_J|_{Y ×_S X} is potentially big over Y.
hypotheses: Maximal variation; g > 1.
proofSteps: By AH.12/potential-bigness-criterion it suffices to prove bigness of the pairings.
(1) (g − 1)π_*⟨i_α^*Θ̄, i_α^*Θ̄⟩ = g d⁴P + d²ι_α^*Θ̄ (AH.9/theta-pullback-formulas) with P nef big (AH.11/bigness-omega-a) and ι_α^*Θ̄ nef.
(2) p₁_*⟨…⟩ = 4g·w + π^*P (AH.9/canonical-theta-identities(2)) with w nef big.
(3) q₁_*⟨…⟩ = 16(g − 1)³Θ̄ + 16g(g − 1)³π_J^*P; Θ̄ is relatively ample and π_J^*P is big from the base, so the sum is big on J.
(4) Restrict (3) to Y: Θ̄|_Y is ample on the generic fibre of Y → T and P|_T is big by maximal variation of T (with dim T in place of dim S, source issue PAPER-YUAN-26/E16).
acceptance: For S = Spec K (dim S = 0) the statements reduce to bigness on the fibre.

nodes.title: Restriction of adelic line bundles across characteristics
nodes.statement: Let S be flat quasi-projective integral over ℤ, L̄ ∈ P̂ic(S/ℤ) and y : Spec K → S with K/k a one-variable function field. Restrict L̄ to S_ℚ/ℚ if char k = 0 or to S_{𝔽_p}/𝔽_p if char k = p, base-change to S_k/k, and pull back to Spec K over k; the degree weights are [k(v) : k]. The same process applies to L̄ on X and its fibre X_y.
hypotheses: S flat over ℤ.
proofSteps: Restriction maps P̂ic(S/ℤ) → P̂ic(S_ℚ/ℚ) and → P̂ic(S_{𝔽_p}/𝔽_p) (forget archimedean and other-prime data; Yuan–Zhang §2.5–2.7), then geometric base change and pullback (AH.1/adelic-line-bundles).
acceptance: For L̄ a model bundle on a projective model over ℤ, the restriction to S_{𝔽_p} is the reduction mod p of the model bundle.

nodes.title: The stable Faltings height over a function field
nodes.statement: Let K/k be a one-variable function field and C/K smooth projective geometrically integral of genus g > 1. Choose a finite K′/K over which C (equivalently J) has semistable reduction everywhere, B′ the regular projective k-curve with function field K′, J′ the Néron model of J_{K′} and e its zero section; put ω_{B′} = e^*Ω^g_{J′/B′} and h_Fal(C) = deg_{B′/k}(ω_{B′})/[K′ : K], with deg_{B′/k}(v) = [k(v) : k] (on Div(B′), source issue E17). It is independent of K′, equals deg(λ_{B′})/[K′ : K] for the Hodge line of the stable model (Pic⁰ of the stable model is the identity component of the Néron model), is ≥ 0, and is > 0 when C_{K̄} is non-isotrivial over k̄, with h_Fal(C) > 3^{−4g²} (char ≠ 3) or > 4^{−4g²} (char 3).
hypotheses: g > 1; K/k of transcendence degree one with k the constant field.
proofSteps: Independence of K′: semistable Néron models commute with base change (NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties).
Hodge comparison: JacobianChallengePartII JC6 with BLR §7.4 Prop. 4 (Yuan pp. 72–73).

Positivity and the explicit lower bound: semistable reduction over the field of N-torsion, N ∈ {3, 4} prime to the characteristic, of degree < N^{4g²}, and integrality of the degree on that field (Yuan Lemma 4.9).
acceptance: For C with everywhere good reduction over k(t) and constant (isotrivial) J, h_Fal = 0.

Over a number field replace deg(v) by log Nv at finite places; at archimedean places φ_v is the archimedean φ (weight 1 or 2), ε_v = 0 and δ_v is Faltings' δ.

nodes.title: Zhang's correction of the canonical self-intersection
nodes.statement: For C with semistable minimal regular model 𝒞: ω_a² = ω²_𝒞 − ε(C), where over number fields ω_𝒞 carries the Arakelov metric. Over a function field, combined with the Noether formula ω²_𝒞 = 12 deg λ − δ(C) = 12h_Fal(C) − δ(C): ω_a² = 12h_Fal(C) − δ(C) − ε(C).
hypotheses: Semistable minimal regular model.
proofSteps: Local comparison of Zhang's admissible metric with the model metric (AH.7/graph-formulas): at each bad place the difference of self-intersections is ε_v (Zhang 1993 Theorem 4.4 as recalled by Yuan).
Noether formula for the semistable fibration over B′ (StableReductionPartII MC.5/integral-noether pulled back) and AH.13/function-field-faltings-height.
acceptance: Good reduction everywhere over a function field: ω_a² = ω²_𝒞 = 12h_Fal.

nodes.title: Lower bounds of ω_a² by φ
nodes.statement: For C/K smooth projective geometrically integral of genus g > 1 over a global field, after a finite extension making C semistable (both sides are invariant under base change with the normalized degrees): (1) ω_a² ≥ ((g − 1)/(2g + 1))φ(C) (Looper–Silverman–Wilms over function fields, with max(2, g − 1) in place of g − 1 and 2(g − 1) in characteristic 0 or for hyperelliptic C; Wilms over number fields). (2) If C is hyperelliptic (in particular g = 2), ω_a² = (2(g − 1)/(2g + 1))φ(C). (3) With A(g) = 1 + (3/(2c(g)) + 2)(2g + 1)/(g − 1) built from the Cinkir constants, A(g) ≤ 139 < 144 for g > 2; for g = 2 the hyperelliptic identity gives the coefficient 1 + (3/(2c(2)) + 2)·(5/2) = 107.25; and 12/A(g) → 12/47.
hypotheses: g > 1; for (2) C hyperelliptic.
proofSteps: (1) Wilms 2022 Theorem 1.2 (number fields) and Looper–Silverman–Wilms Proposition 6.1 (function fields).
(2) Zhang 2010 Corollary 1.3.3: the Gross–Schoen cycle of a hyperelliptic curve vanishes (AH.10/gross-schoen-variation).
acceptance: A(4) = 1 + (44 + 2)·3 = 139 exactly; the g = 2 coefficient 107.25 = 1 + 42.5·2.5 (both checked in the suggested Lean file).

Gives the hyperelliptic identity.

nodes.title: Comparison of ω_a² with the Faltings height over function fields
nodes.statement: Let K/k be a one-variable function field and C/K smooth projective geometrically integral of genus g > 1, K′/K finite with a semistable minimal regular model C′ over the regular projective k-curve S′ of K′. Then (1/12)h_Fal(C) ≤ ω²_{C/K,a} ≤ ω²_{C′/S′}/[K′ : K] ≤ 12h_Fal(C). If moreover C_{K̄} is non-isotrivial over k̄, then (1/12)max{h_Fal(C), 4^{−4g²}} ≤ ω²_{C/K,a} ≤ 12max{h_Fal(C), 1}.
hypotheses: g > 1; K/k one-variable function field.
proofSteps: Base change to K′ and write ω_a² = 12h_Fal − δ − ε (AH.13/zhang-correction); upper bounds from δ, ε ≥ 0.

Lower bound: ε ≤ δ/2 + 2φ (AH.10/graph-invariant-inequalities(5)) and δ ≤ φ/c(g) give δ + ε ≤ (3/(2c(g)) + 2)φ ≤ (3/(2c(g)) + 2)((2g + 1)/(g − 1))ω_a² = (A(g) − 1)ω_a² by AH.13/phi-lower-bounds(1); hence 12h_Fal = ω_a² + δ + ε ≤ A(g)ω_a² ≤ 139ω_a² for g > 2, and ≤ 107.25ω_a² for g = 2 by the hyperelliptic identity, so ω_a² ≥ h_Fal/12 (Yuan pp. 86–88).
Non-isotrivial case: AH.13/function-field-faltings-height lower bound 3^{−4g²} or 4^{−4g²} ≥ 4^{−4g²}.

Alternative weaker route: the slope inequality ω²_{C/S} ≥ (4 − 4/g)deg λ_S for semistable fibrations (Cornalba–Harris, Xiao; Moriwaki in positive characteristic — its generality is not verified here, Yuan Remark 4.12(2)).
acceptance: Everywhere good reduction: ω_a² = 12h_Fal, consistent with both inequalities.

nodes.title: Wilms' lower bound for Faltings' δ
nodes.statement: For every compact connected Riemann surface X of genus g ≥ 1, δ(X) > −2g log(2π⁴).
proofSteps: From Wilms' formula (AH.10/faltings-delta) using ∫_{Pic^{g−1}} log‖θ‖ ν^g/g! < −(g/4)log 2 (Jensen) and φ(X) ≥ 0 (Wilms Corollary 1.2).
acceptance: g = 1: −2 log(2π⁴) ≈ −10.54 < −9, consistent with Faltings' δ > −9.

nodes.title: Bost's lower bound for the Faltings height, in Faltings' normalization
nodes.statement: For a principally polarized abelian variety (in particular a Jacobian) of dimension g over ℚ̄, the stable Faltings height in Faltings' normalization ‖α‖² = (i^{g²}/2^g)∫α∧ᾱ satisfies h_Fal ≥ −(g/2)log(2π²); in Deligne's normalization h_Del ≥ −(g/2)log(2π). Hence for M̄ = Θ̄ + π_J^*λ̄_S + O(c) with c = (g/2)log(2π²) + 1, h_M̄(y) = 2ĥ(y) + h_Fal(X_s) + c ≥ 2ĥ(y) + max{h_Fal(X_s), 1}, since h_Fal + c ≥ 1 always and h_Fal + c ≥ h_Fal.
hypotheses: Number fields; Faltings normalization as in Yuan §4.3.1.
proofSteps: Import ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights R35.6 §6.5 (Bost's theorem, Gaudron–Rémond Corollary 8.4) and the normalization shift h_Fal = h_Del − (g/2) log π of R35.2 §2.7.

Yuan p. 78 quotes −g log √(2π) = −(g/2)log(2π), Deligne's form, while using Faltings' metric (pp. 43–44, 73); the corrected constant is recorded as source issue ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeightsPartII/E1. The argument only needs some uniform constant, so the conclusion is unaffected.
acceptance: g = 1: the minimum of h_Del is ≈ −0.749 at j = 0 (Deligne), so min h_Fal ≈ −0.749 − (1/2)log π ≈ −1.321, below −(1/2)log(2π) ≈ −0.919 but above −(1/2)log(2π²) ≈ −1.491.

sources.match: Quotes Bost's lower bound to choose the constant c in M = Θ̄ + π_J^*λ̄_S + O(c), with the Faltings metric of §4.3.1; item PAPER-YUAN-26/144.

nodes.title: The boundary-coercive divisor for the lower height estimate
nodes.statement: Fix a Cinkir constant c(g) > 0. In the arithmetic curve-moduli setting (fine level moduli over ℤ[1/N] with a stable compactification of its generic fibre) put D_S = (3/(2c(g)) + 3)Φ_S − Ξ_S ∈ D̂iv(S/ℤ)_ℚ. Its geometric part D̃ satisfies D̃ − c(g)Δ ≥ 0 over S_ℚ/ℚ, and its archimedean Green function tends to +∞ at the boundary of moduli, hence is bounded below by a constant c₅′(g).
hypotheses: g > 1; fine level moduli with stable compactification.
proofSteps: Geometric part: Φ̃ has Green function φ(Γ_v), Ξ̃ has δ(Γ_v) + ε(Γ_v) (AH.10/noether-divisor); ε ≤ δ/2 + 2φ and φ ≥ c(g)δ give (3/(2c) + 3)φ − δ − ε ≥ c(g)δ (the coefficient c(g)Δ, not Δ: source issue PAPER-YUAN-26/E25).
Archimedean coercivity: as in AH.11/uniform-phi-bound, effectivity of the geometric part over (ℂ, |·|) forces the Green function to grow at the boundary; with Wilms' δ bound it is bounded below.
acceptance: For c(g) = 1/25 the coefficient is 3·25/2 + 3 = 40.5.

nodes.title: Comparison of ω_a² with the Faltings height over number fields
nodes.statement: For g > 1 there is c₅(g) ∈ ℝ such that for every smooth projective geometrically connected C/K of genus g over a number field, with K′/K any finite extension over which C has a semistable minimal regular model C′: max{h_Fal(C)/12 + c₅, ((g − 1)/(2g + 1))c₀} ≤ [ω²_{C/K,a}] ≤ [ω²_{C′/O_{K′},Ar}] ≤ 12h_Fal(C) + 6g log(2π²), where [·] divides by the degree over ℚ and c₀ = c₀(g) is the constant of AH.11/uniform-phi-bound. The constant c₅ is not claimed positive or effective.
hypotheses: g > 1; number fields.
proofSteps: (a) Wilms: ω_a² ≥ ((g − 1)/(2g + 1))φ(C); φ_v ≥ 0 at finite places and φ_σ ≥ c₀ at archimedean places.

(b) Write 12λ̄ − P = O(Ξ_S) on fine moduli and use the coercive divisor (AH.13/boundary-coercive-divisor): (3/(2c) + 3)P ≥ ... gives [ω_a²] ≥ h_Fal/12 + c₅ (Yuan pp. 93–95, with the λ̄_{O_K} reading of source issue E30).
(c) ω_a² ≤ ω²_Ar since ε ≥ 0; arithmetic Noether with Wilms' δ > −2g log(2π⁴): ω²_Ar = 12 deĝλ̄ − δ + 4g[K:ℚ]log 2π ≤ 12h_Fal[K:ℚ] + 2g log(2π⁴)[K:ℚ] + 4g log(2π)[K:ℚ] = [K:ℚ](12h_Fal + 6g log(2π²)).
acceptance: Constant check: 2g log(2π⁴) + 4g log(2π) = 2g log(8π⁶) = 6g log(2π²).

Supplies ω̂² ≥ ((g − 1)/(2g + 1))φ.

nodes.title: Uniform comparison of [ω_a²] with max{h_Fal, 1}
nodes.statement: For each g > 1 there are c₃(g), c₄(g) > 0 such that for every number field or one-variable function field K/k and every smooth projective geometrically connected curve C/K of genus g, non-isotrivial over k̄ in the function-field case, c₃·max{h_Fal(C), 1} ≤ [ω²_{C/K,a}] ≤ c₄·max{h_Fal(C), 1}, with [·] dividing by [K : ℚ] in the number-field case only.

gaps.title: G1. Wazir's Silverman–Tate and specialization theorems for Moriwaki heights

gaps.title: G2. Bedford–Taylor products on singular complex projective varieties
gaps.detail: Yuan–Zhang §2.1.1 obtains Monge–Ampère measures of integrable continuous metrics on (possibly singular) complex projective varieties from Bedford–Taylor (and Demailly), and semipositivity comparisons from Coman–Guedj–Zeriahi Corollary C. gaps.title: G3. Arithmetic Noether formula
gaps.detail: Faltings, Calculus on arithmetic surfaces (Ann. of Math. 119, 1984), Theorem 6, and Moret-Bailly, La formule de Noether pour les surfaces arithmétiques (Invent. Math. 98, 1989), Théorème 2.5, were not read; the constant 4g log 2π and the normalization of δ are taken from Yuan p. 89 and are consistent with Wilms' formula. gaps.title: G4. Gross–Schoen height of the modified diagonal
gaps.detail: The unconditional height of Δ_ξ uses Gross–Schoen's regular-model construction (Gross–Schoen 1995, Ann. Inst. Fourier), recalled in Zhang 2010 §1.1 but not read in the original; no general Beilinson–Bloch pairing is assumed.

gaps.title: G5. Boundary growth of φ and δ from graph data
gaps.detail: Yuan Remarks 3.11 and 4.13(2) assert, without proof, that the adelic divisors Φ̃ and Ξ̃ describe the growth of φ and of Faltings' δ at the boundary of complex moduli (compare Song 2023 and de Jong 2019). These are not targets of this roadmap.

gaps.title: G6. Cinkir's genus-three constant
gaps.detail: c(3) = 17/288 is from Cinkir, Admissible invariants of genus 3 curves (Manuscripta Math. 148, 2015), p. 318 (iv), not read. The arXiv v2 bound t(3) = (892 − 11√79)/14580 ≈ 0.0545 of Cinkir 2011 Theorem 2.9 gives A(3) ≤ 1 + (3/(2·0.0545) + 2)·3.5 ≈ 104.3 < 139, so the conclusion A(g) ≤ 139 does not depend on it.

gaps.title: G7. Genus one
gaps.detail: Yuan states Theorem 2.3 and Theorem A.1 for g > 0, but the normalization and nefness are proved only for g > 1 (PAPER-YUAN-26/E8, E28). Every target of this roadmap assumes g > 1.

sourceIssues.locator: §4.4.1, p. 78 (author manuscript of 21 August 2024), read with §4.3.1, p. 73 and Lemma 3.4, pp. 43–44
sourceIssues.printed: Yuan quotes Bost's explicit bound as h_Fal(X_s) ≥ −g log √(2π) and takes c = g log √(2π) + 1, while defining h_Fal with the Faltings metric ‖α‖² = (i^{g²}/2^g)∫α∧ᾱ.
sourceIssues.correction: In the Faltings normalization Bost's theorem gives h_Fal ≥ −(g/2)log(2π²) = −g log(π√2); the bound −(g/2)log(2π) is Bost's bound in Deligne's normalization (2π)^{−g}|∫α∧ᾱ|. Take c = (g/2)log(2π²) + 1.
sourceIssues.reason: h_Fal = h_Del − (g/2)log π (ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights R35.2 §2.7) and Bost: h_Del ≥ −(g/2)log(2π) (R35.6 §6.5). For g = 1 the printed inequality fails for abelian varieties: the minimum of h_Del over elliptic curves is about −0.749 at j = 0, so min h_Fal ≈ −1.321 < −(1/2)log(2π) ≈ −0.919. Yuan himself remarks that constants differ between normalizations.
